answer: The canyon cap is enforced at intake and comet shows the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a dune tag. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 5 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
